survey: A wooden barrel stands upright on a plank floor, seen from slightly above and in front. Vertical staves make up a body that bulges at the middle and narrows evenly toward the top and bottom. Four dark iron hoops go all the way round: one just under the top chime, one at the upper quarter, one at the lower quarter and one at the base. Each hoop has one rivet facing the camera. The staves run straight through the hoops, and their seams line up from one section to the next. At the top, the stave ends rise into a chime rim, and a flat head made of boards sits recessed inside it. The bottom hoop meets the floor, and a contact shadow falls to the right, so the barrel truly rests on the surface. The small orange splat on one stave is surface decoration, not a structural part. The barrel is simplified, but every part is correct: the hoops sit tight on the curve, the head is held by the chime, and the barrel could hold liquid and stand.
